summary: GT23 published moments (N*m/kg) were not divided by the participant's own mass in most subjects, and the divisor can change between trials of one subject. Evidence 1 (exact): RawData/<subj>/MotionFile_EH/inverse_dynamics.sto (local N*m inverse dynamics, NOT in the publisher archive directory, provenance unknown) equals the published normal_walk_1 moments times a constant (corr 1.0; max residual 0.0-0.03 N*m in AB01/05/06/08/10/12, 0.2-0.4 AB09, 3.5-4.7 AB13 on p99 100-260 N*m) for 8 subjects. Divisors: AB01 78.9 (own), AB05 78.9 (own 71.5), AB06 71.5 (own 79.1), AB08 62.3 (own 87.6), AB09 87.57 (own 84.1), AB10 84.1 (own 67.5), AB12 65.1 (own 64.0), AB13 64.0 (own 67.6). Evidence 2 (independent, mass-free): force-plate lever-arm moment in the calcn frame with joint centres/axes from each trial's own scaled model (Statics.csv; foot is unscaled in every used model, so ankle = generic 0.04877/0.04195 m; knee uses the subject's tibia length and Joint_Angle ankle/subtalar angles). The lever-arm bias (0.9942, robust sd 0.015 log) was calibrated on 5 of the 8 re-run trials (AB01, AB06, AB09, AB12, AB13); out of sample it held on 3 of 3 (AB05 2.1 %, AB08 1.3 %, AB10 4.9 %, the last at the band edge). It tracks the exact divisor, not the README mass (fig 3). Lever-arm level-walk divisors for the other subjects: AB02 82.1 (own 82.2), AB03 82.6 (own 113.5; AB02's 82.2), AB07 76.6 (own 62.3; AB06's 79.1), AB11 67.3 (own 65.1 / AB10's 67.5, ambiguous). README masses are true body masses (force plates within 1 % in 12/12; model masses equal README). Established counts: the level-walk divisor is not the subject's own mass in 9 of 12 subjects (AB03, AB05, AB06, AB07, AB08, AB09, AB10, AB12, AB13). In 7 of them a re-run fixes it at another subject's README table mass (AB05 78.9 = AB01; AB06 71.5; AB08 62.3; AB10 84.1; AB12 65.1 exact, residual 0.0-0.03 N*m; AB09 87.57 and AB13 64.0 near-exact, residual 0.2-0.4 and 3.5-4.7 N*m). In 6 of these it is the previous subject in README order (AB06, AB08, AB09, AB10, AB12, AB13); AB05's level walk uses AB01's mass instead. AB03 and AB07 are force-plate only and not unique: AB03 82.6 fits 82.2 (AB02) or 84.1 (AB09), and within this worker's +/-4.9 % band also 78.9 and 79.1; AB07 76.6 fits 79.1 (AB06) or 78.9 (AB01). Both clearly exclude their own mass (113.5, 62.3). AB01 is correct (own 78.9, exact); AB02 and AB11 cannot be told apart from own vs another mass at 5 %. AB05 incline_walk_1, incline_walk_2, turn_and_step_1 and dynamic_walk_1 use about 113-118 kg (consistent with AB03's 113.5; ankle and knee agree). The exact divisors are the one-decimal table values (AB06 71.5 gives 0.0 N*m residual; AB05's model mass 71.541 gives 0.09-0.14), consistent with a table lookup offset; the mechanism is not established. Published values are 0.61-1.46 times the correctly normalized per-kg value over 52 trials with ankle corr >= 0.98 (subject level-walk factors: AB03 1.375, AB05 0.906 [0.63 in incline/turn/dynamic], AB06 1.106, AB07 0.814, AB08 1.406, AB09 0.960, AB10 0.803, AB12 0.983, AB13 1.056). Trial outliers confirmed by ankle and knee besides AB05: AB12 cutting_1 (~82.6 kg vs 65.1) and AB13 tire_run_1 (~77 kg vs 64.0); cause not identified. Curb trials give unreliable lever estimates (ankle corr < 0.98 in 6 of 9). Prior C02 findings explained: AB03 78-85 kg is consistent with AB02's 82.2 kg but not unique (not the AB02 model file: its tibia lengths differ from AB02's own model, and the file is unused per Statics.csv); AB05 incline_walk_2 114-120 kg is consistent with AB03's 113.5 kg; AB10 1.33x = 84.1/67.5 = 1.25 (exact); AB08 0.73x = 62.3/87.6 = 0.71 (exact). Nothing rescaled or excluded. Handling drafted as decision D-GT23-C03-1.

verdict.mis_scaled_subjects: Not own mass at level walking: 9 of 12 (AB03, AB05, AB06, AB07, AB08, AB09, AB10, AB12, AB13). Another subject's table mass fixed by re-run: 7 (AB05, AB06, AB08, AB10, AB12 exact; AB09, AB13 near-exact). Previous subject in README order: 6 (AB06, AB08, AB09, AB10, AB12, AB13). AB03 and AB07 force-plate only, not unique. AB01 correct; AB02 and AB11 not distinguishable at 5 %.
verdict.per_trial: Divisor varies within subject: AB05 (78.9 level walk vs 113-118 in 4 other trials); AB12 cutting_1 and AB13 tire_run_1 differ from the subject's walking divisor by 1.27x and 1.21x (ankle and knee agree). Only 4-6 trials per subject were tested.
verdict.likely_cause: Normalization used another subject's mass-table value (one-decimal table values, not model masses): the previous subject in README order in 6 of 7 re-run-fixed cases, with AB05's level walk = AB01's mass as an exception. README masses, force plates and models agree with each other, so the error is in the authors' division step, not the mass table or the AB02 model file in AB03's folder. The mechanism (e.g., an indexing error) is not established.
verdict.powers: Joint_Powers share the moment normalization (C02), so they inherit the same factors (not re-tested here).

tolerance.pre_registered_v1: Fixed in the reference stage before test-subject data were read: log(implied/README) over reference seeded trials, centre 1.034, band 0.868-1.232 (3 robust sd). Reported in the audit as flags_v1_readme_band. Superseded as the primary rule because the reference subjects themselves turned out to be mis-normalized (exact re-run divisors differ from README in AB06/09/12/13), so README agreement is not a valid reference.
tolerance.v2: Added after the reference stage, before any test-subject (AB03/05/08/10) data were read (timestamps in the audit): lever-arm calibrated against the 5 reference subjects with exact re-run divisors (AB01/06/09/12/13 normal_walk_1): bias 0.9942, half width max(3 x 0.0152, log 1.05) = 0.0488 log (about +/-5 %). Trial band: within-subject deviation from the subject's level-walk lever estimate, robust sd 0.028, half width log 1.10.
tolerance.honesty_note: v2 was introduced after seeing reference-subject results, not test-subject results. The test was not blind: the test subjects (AB03, AB05, AB08, AB10) were chosen because they were the known GT23-C02 anomalies, so their direction was known in advance. The audit's tolerance timestamps (tolerance_fixed_at_utc 06:43:02, tolerance_v2_fixed_at_utc 06:43:04, finished 06:43:11) come from the final rerun of all three stages only; they show ordering within that run, not that test data were unseen during development. During development, reference and calibrate ran before any test-subject read, and the tolerance rules were not changed after test results were seen. The exact re-run divisors do not depend on any tolerance; tolerance affects only the force-plate-only subjects (AB02, AB03, AB07, AB11) and the trial flags.

decisions.question: GT23 joint moments and powers were divided by another participant's body mass in most subjects, and the mass can change between trials of one participant. How should LocoHub release GT23 moments and powers?

options.label: Withhold GT23 moments and powers
options.consequence: Kinematics and forces still released; no GT23 joint kinetics until the authors confirm the masses or a full check is reviewed. Nothing is estimated. Reversible.

options.label: Rescale each trial to its participant's own mass
options.consequence: Needs a full per-trial check first: each trial's divisor is measured (exact where an N·m re-run matches the published values by a constant, else force plates within 5 %) and matched to a recorded mass; unmatched trials are left out. Adds a derived step that needs its own review. Reversible.

options.label: Release as published with an erratum
options.consequence: All values kept with a per-subject warning table; users get moments and powers 0.61 to 1.46 times the per-kg value and must correct them. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By GT23 moment trials released: none, only those with a matched divisor, all.
decisions.why: An N·m re-run fixes the divisor in 8 level-walking trials; in 7 it is another participant's mass, and the divisor changes between trials of one subject, so a correction needs a divisor for every trial. Withholding invents nothing and is reversed once a full check or the authors confirm the masses.

decisions.cost_of_waiting: GT23 joint kinetics stay out of any release and drafts keep the published mis-scaled values; GT23 kinematics and other datasets are unaffected.
